findings.issue: `pkill -f "entry.node-server"` matches the agent's own bash command line and SIGTERMs its own shell (exit 143); this happened at turns 58, 61, 77, and again on the final turn 81, twice discarding the result of a chained test run.
findings.suggestion: Kill by recorded PID (/tmp/app.pid, already written) or by port (fuser -k 3000/tcp), or use a pkill pattern that cannot appear in the shell's own argv; apply the turn-63 setsid recipe consistently.

findings.issue: Turns 44-46 spent three calls re-grepping freshly written files for typos ('</d>', 'for=') that were never actually made, with no failing signal prompting it.
findings.suggestion: Trust the write result and the typecheck/build; only re-inspect code in response to an actual error.

findings.issue: Combined `npm run build && pkill ... ; npm test` into one command; when pkill killed the shell, the build output was lost and the test never ran, wasting the turn.
findings.suggestion: Don't chain a test run behind a risky kill command; run the kill in its own call.

findings.issue: Smoke-test probe crashed with a Python AttributeError on the 301 empty body of /pokemon/pikachu instead of surfacing the redirect.
findings.suggestion: Check the HTTP status code before parsing the body in probe scripts (it did get this right one turn later with curl -i).

findings.issue: Several thinking blocks are extremely large (25k-49k chars; 168k total), inflating cost/latency without changing any decision.
findings.suggestion: Compress the long pre-implementation design notes; most of their content could have been settled in half the tokens.

summary: An exceptionally well-planned session: 29 turns of up-front reconnaissance (spec, all tests, data shapes with overlay, all reference screenshots, verified framework version via npm dist-tags) led to the entire app being written in one pass with the 54-test suite passing on the very first run and again after the final edit. Verification went beyond the tests — browser screenshots compared against every reference design, plus manual edge-case and 404 probes. The only recurring flaw is operational: a self-matching pkill pattern killed the agent's own shell four times, including on the last turn.
